properties.name: Coyote Steals Fire
properties.summary: In many Native American traditions, Coyote stole fire from the Fire Spirits to give to humanity. Through cunning and relay races with other animals, the fire was passed until it reached humanity. Coyote's cleverness is balanced by his foolishness. He is both creator and destroyer, teacher and troublemaker.

properties.name: Raven Steals the Light
properties.summary: In the beginning, the world was dark. The Sky Chief kept the sun, moon, and stars in bentwood boxes. Raven transformed into a pine needle, was swallowed by the chief's daughter, and was reborn as her grandson. As a child, he opened the boxes one by one, releasing light into the world.

properties.name: White Buffalo Calf Woman
properties.summary: Two Lakota warriors encountered a beautiful woman in white. One approached with desire and was reduced to bones. The other was respectful. She brought the sacred pipe (chanunpa), teaching seven sacred rites including the Sun Dance, vision quest, and sweat lodge. She transformed into a white buffalo calf and vanished.

properties.name: Sedna — Mistress of the Sea
properties.summary: Sedna was a beautiful Inuit woman tricked into marrying a bird spirit. Her father Anguta rescued her by kayak, but a storm threatened to capsize them. He threw Sedna overboard; when she clung to the boat, he cut off her fingers. Her fingers became seals, walruses, and whales. She sank to rule the sea floor.

properties.name: Navajo Emergence — Four Worlds
properties.summary: The Navajo people emerged through four colored worlds — Black, Blue, Yellow, and White. In each world, conflicts caused by Coyote forced migration upward. Spider Woman taught weaving; First Man and First Woman brought sacred medicine bundles. Through a reed, the people climbed into the Fifth World — the present glittering world.

properties.name: Corn Mother — Gift of Agriculture
properties.summary: In Penobscot tradition, Corn Mother arose from corn silk and married First Father. When famine came, she instructed her sons to kill her and drag her body over bare ground. From her flesh grew corn; from her bones grew tobacco. She sacrificed herself so her people would never go hungry.
